sec: Sinusoidal vasoconstriction and the HVPG ladder · p1002

items.q: In the equation P = F × R used on p1002 for portal HTN, a rise in sinusoidal resistance leads to:
opts: Fall in flow at fixed pressure
Rise in flow for fixed resistance
items.exp: Resistance due to: (P = F × R; R↑ = P↑). (Book p1002)

items.q: Match the HVPG (hepatic venous pressure gradient) ladder of p1002 — 1) 1–5 mm Hg  2) ≥ 10 mm Hg  3) ≥ 12 mm Hg  4) ≥ 20 mm Hg … A) Threshold pressure for variceal rupture  B) Normal value  C) ↑ Risk of death  D) Clinically significant portal hypertension
items.exp: HVPG table: 1–5 mm Hg = normal value; ≥ 10 mm Hg = clinically significant portal hypertension; ≥ 12 mm Hg = threshold pressure for variceal rupture; ≥ 20 mm Hg = ↑ risk of death. (Book p1002)

items.q: The HVPG that marks the threshold pressure for variceal rupture is:
items.exp: ≥ 12 mm Hg is labelled the threshold pressure for variceal rupture. (Book p1002)

items.q: A cirrhotic patient's HVPG is measured at 11 mm Hg. According to the p1002 ladder, the best interpretation is:
opts: Clinically significant portal hypertension, but below the printed variceal-rupture threshold
Normal — HVPG must reach 12 mm Hg before portal hypertension is significant
Already within the ≥ 20 mm Hg band that marks an increased risk of death
Indeterminate — the 10–12 mm Hg gap on the ladder carries no printed label
items.exp: ≥ 10 mm Hg = clinically significant portal hypertension; ≥ 12 mm Hg = threshold for variceal rupture; so 11 sits between the two printed marks. (Book p1002)

items.q: The functional (non-mechanical) cause of sinusoidal vasoconstriction in portal HTN is a fall in:
items.exp: Functional cause: ↓ intrasinusoidal NO → contraction of sinusoid → defenestration. (Book p1002)

items.q: ‘In sinusoidal vasoconstriction, the NO pathway causes the sinusoid to relax.’
opts: False — ↓ intrasinusoidal NO causes contraction of the sinusoid
True — NO mediates sinusoidal relaxation here
False — the cause is a rise, not a fall, in NO
True, but only in the presinusoidal segment
items.exp: Functional cause: ↓ intrasinusoidal NO → contraction of sinusoid → defenestration. (Book p1002)

items.q: The mechanical cause of sinusoidal resistance in portal HTN, as drawn on p1002, is:
opts: Spasm of the portal vein wall
items.exp: Mechanical cause: nodule compressing sinusoid (functional arm is the ↓ NO pathway). (Book p1002)

items.q: All but one of the following appear in the p1002 functional-cause chain (↓ intrasinusoidal NO → …). The odd one out is:
items.exp: The chain is ↓ intrasinusoidal NO → contraction of sinusoid → defenestration; portal vein thrombosis is not part of it. (Book p1002)
